# bugs #3885: mcs51: pushing a struct argument with r0 and r1 in use leaves an extra byte on the stack

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3885/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Choose between this patch and the wider patch in the eighth comment of bug #4131. The patch for bug #3395 depends on this change.
- Patch: [bugs-3885.patch](../../patches/bugs-3885.patch), commit [`2495c07b5`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/2495c07b5a660bd9ac1e5cfe91984133240d55c7). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

In trunk a guard that names this ticket disables `tests/dynamiccstructret.c.in` for mcs51 with
`--stack-auto`. After the guard is removed, the test fails on r17158 for mcs51-small-stack-auto
and mcs51-large-stack-auto. The failure does not depend on `__dynamicc`. It occurs when the caller
pushes a struct argument by value while r0 and r1 both hold values that are needed later.

## Cause

`genPointerPush` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` generates the code for `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS`, which pushes
a struct argument byte by byte. When the struct is addressed through a one-byte pointer,
`genPointerPush` requests a pointer register from `getFreePtr`. When r0 and r1 are both in use,
`getFreePtr` saves one of them. For `IPUSH` and `PCALL` it copies the register to B. For every
other operation it pushes the register, and in trunk `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` is one of the other
operations.

The byte that `getFreePtr` pushes is then on the stack below the argument bytes. `genPointerPush`
calls `freeAsmop` with `pop` false, so no instruction removes it. After the call, the caller pops
its registers from positions that are one byte too high, and the stack pointer stays one byte
above its value before the call sequence.

## Fix

`getFreePtr` treats `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` as it treats `IPUSH` and `PCALL`. It copies the
register to B, and `freeAsmop` restores it with `mov r0,b` or `mov r1,b`. The loop in
`genPointerPush` that pushes the bytes uses only A and the pointer register. The patch also removes
the guard from the test.

## Decision

The patch changes `getFreePtr` alone. That corrects the push when one of the two registers is
saved, which is the case of the test.

The mcs51 patch in the sixth comment of bug #4131 has the same two hunks. A maintainer answered
there that it is insufficient, because the compiler then tries to save both r0 and r1 in B. Each
call of `getFreePtr` that finds both registers in use saves one of them in B. `aopForSym` calls it
for an operand that is addressed through r0 or r1, such as an operand on the stack with
`--stack-auto`, and `genPointerPush` calls it for the register that addresses the struct. When
both calls occur for one `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` and each saves a register, the second copy to B
replaces the first. This case was read from the source. It was not tested with this patch.

The alternative is the mcs51 patch in the eighth comment of bug #4131. It has the two hunks of
this patch. It also changes `genPointerPush`, which then releases the source operand before it
requests the pointer register and keeps the value in B while the tag of a generic pointer is
loaded. It adds `tests/mcs51-aggregate-argument.c` for the two stack-auto targets. Its author
reports in the ninth comment that the regression suite passes for those targets. That patch was
read for this report and was not built.

## Verification

After the guard is removed, `tests/dynamiccstructret.c.in` fails for mcs51-small-stack-auto and
mcs51-large-stack-auto without the patch and passes for both with it.

## Related

Bug #3395 is the failure of `gte/pr30185.c` for the two stack-auto targets. That test passes with
this patch.
